ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 16-07; mandatory sanctions screening against UN Security Council resolutions, EU Council regulations, FSA lists, and an accepted US OFAC catch-all protocol for non-EU jurisdictions; screening must be risk-based, on-going, and documented at pre-incorporation and continuously during the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin characters; non-Latin script names require a transliteration in the statutory deed. The name must be unambiguous, distinguishable from existing trademark/entity names, and not contrary to public policy. Administrative documents are prepared in French, German, or Luxembourgish, with French being standard for notarial deeds.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank / Banque / Banker (requires CSSF prior license)
Insurance / Assurance / Réassurance (requires CAA prior license)
Luxembourg / State / Finance Ministry (requires ministerial authorization)
SICAV / SICAR / SICAF / FCP / Fonds (requires CSSF fund authorization)
Tax Haven / Offshore / Fake terms inconsistent with commercial substance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written re-examination request with the RCSL within 15 days. If re-examination fails, an administrative appeal can be lodged with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months, pursuant to Code administratif provisions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as a substitute for a physical registered office for the SCSp; a service address located at a law firm or corporate services provider in Luxembourg is accepted only if it constitutes a genuine, locally administered registered office with physical capacity to receive legal process, retain corporate records, and conduct day-to-day administrative meetings.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% over the first three years, increasing to 30% if the SCSp engages in intra-group financing or holds tax repartition rulings; unannounced inspections may be conducted by the tax authorities (ACD), RCSL, and AML supervisors.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 101-123 (SCSp regime inserted by the Law of 23 July 2016); amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies, Articles 1, 3, 8 and 11
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 9-12 Boulevard F.D. Roosevelt, L-2450 Luxembourg; online via the e-RCS portal (lbr.lu)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société / Statuts) filed together with the electronic registration declaration (proposition de dépôt) in accordance with RCS procedural forms
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital applies to an SCSp; the partnership agreement freely determines capital contributions (cash or in kind). No statutory escrow or bank attestation is required unless real estate is contributed, in which case a notarial deed is mandatory.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole general partner of [●] SCSp, a special limited partnership organised under the laws of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, hereby: (1) APPROVES the capital subscription of EUR [●] set out in the partnership agreement dated [●], such subscription being granted, accepted and recorded in the partners' register; (2) ADOPTS as the partnership's registered office the premises at [●], Grand-Duchy of Luxembourg; and (3) APPOINTS [●] as Manager (Gérant), with authority to represent the partnership, open bank accounts, sign regulatory filings, and approve any amendments to the registrations before the Luxembourg Business Registers. All acts performed by the Manager prior to this resolution are hereby ratified. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and optional notarisation of the SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners themselves by private deed; Luxembourg notary mandatory only if real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement (statuts/contrat de société) in French or English containing the corporate name, registered office, corporate objects (manufacture of ultra-high-definition rigid endoscopes and laparoscopy towers), duration, capital, and the rights of the general and limited partners. Execute the deed by all partners or before a Luxembourg notary where immovable property is contributed. Have signature pages certified and append the manager's specimen signature.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement
Copy of passports of all general and limited partners
Proof of business address (lease agreement, ownership title, or domiciliation letter)
Manager's specimen signature and consent to appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any partner's signature is challenged or defective, rectify the deed and re-execute; if the notary refuses approval, adjust the contribution terms to exclude real estate and proceed by private deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS registration of the SCSp and allotment of the registration number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS, via e-RCS online filing portal or RCS desk in Luxembourg City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the e-RCS portal and complete the electronic registration declaration; attach the signed partnership agreement, proof of registered office, partner identity documents, and the manager's appointment and specimen signature. Pay the EUR 24 registration fee online. The RCS will allot the registration number and issue the certificate of registration (extrait/attestation).
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (scanned copy)
Electronic registration declaration (proposition de dépôt)
Proof of registered office address
Identity documents of general and limited partners
Consent and specimen signature of the appointed manager
Notarial copy of the deed if notarised
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query (demande de complément), correct and resubmit the electronic file within the prescribed delay (typically 15 days); obtain assistance from the RCS helpdesk or a Luxembourg counsel to cure deficiencies and avoid rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory publication of the incorporation in the RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mémorial - Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA), official electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon completion of RCS registration, the RCS transmits the deed for RESA publication. Verify the draft published extract for accuracy of the company name, registered office, object, capital, and manager details. The EUR 75 publication fee is invoiced by the LBR/RESA service. Publication confers legal effect of the constitution vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration confirmation
Legalised copy of the partnership agreement
Proof of payment of publication fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published extract contains typographical or legal errors, file a request with the RCS/Mémorial for corrective re-publication; corrections are published in the next RESA update and notified to the registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: TVA (VAT) registration and obtention of the autorisation d'établissement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Ministry of the Economy - Directorate-General for Industry, Service des autorisations d'établissement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the common registration form (formulaire 10) to the AEDT within 15 days of RCS registration together with the RCS extract to obtain the Luxembourg TVA number. Concurrently file the business establishment licence application under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 for the regulated manufacture of medical devices, attaching the manager's diploma or proof of at least 3 years' professional experience, criminal record extract, and the planned EU MDR conformity assessment documentation; pay the EUR 95 application fee.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Identification forms of partners and managers
Criminal record extract (extrait de casier judiciaire)
Diploma or proof of 3 years professional experience
EU MDR (Regulation 2017/745) manufacturer registration data and conformity assessment plan
Payment proof of EUR 95 fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of refusal or query, file a recours with the Ministry of the Economy within 40 days, or an administrative appeal before the Luxembourg administrative tribunal; supplement missing professional evidence or revise the business description to match ISIC 3250.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer affiliation with the CCSS and ITM occupational notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS using the declaration d'entrée en activité to obtain the social security affiliation number and enrol any employees. Notify the ITM of the establishment's opening, of the clean-room operations, and of any laser or optical radiation equipment; arrange the mandatory pre-opening workplace inspection where staff are hired.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
TVA certificate
Copy of the autorisation d'établissement
Staff list and declaration of entry into activity
ITM notification form for workplace and equipment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any data discrepancies promptly through the CCSS portal; if the ITM raises health and safety findings, implement corrective measures (e.g., electrical, laser, or clean-room ventilation upgrades) and request a follow-up inspection before production launch.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate-General for Industry (Service des autorisations d'établissement); Ministry of Health - Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments (EU MDR manufacturer registration)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (business establishment licence) pursuant to the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of craftsman, merchant, industrialist and to certain liberal professions; medical device manufacturer registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR), Article 31

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 'établissement classé' - comparative screening notice required under Annex II of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; no full EIA report is expected for a low-emission clean-room endoscope assembly line; communal building and operating permits (permis de construire / permis d'exploiter) remain mandatory
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge limits per Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 July 1994 and communal sewer ordinances: pH 6.5-9.5, COD ≤ 1,000 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 400 mg/L, TSS ≤ 400 mg/L, aluminium/copper/zinc below 2 mg/L; VOC emissions from solvent-based cleaning subject to Directive 1999/13/EC where annual solvent consumption exceeds 1 tonne; hazardous waste (isopropanol, glutaraldehyde disinfectants) segregated and managed under the Law of 21 March 2012; HEPA-filtered clean-room exhaust complying with EU MDR environmental controls

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) and the commune; structural stability and load certificate issued by an approved civil engineering office; occupational health and safety approval from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering electrical installations, laser eye-safety per IEC/EN 60825-1, and clean-room sterile packaging operations

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Luxembourg VAT, registration and indirect tax authority; operational portal: MyGuichet.lu / Guichet Public (https://guichet.public.lu); direct tax counterpart: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); customs and EORI matters: Administration des douanes et accises (Luxembourg Customs and Excise).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Obtain the Luxembourg national business registration number ('matricule') from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — required before VAT registration for any non-resident entity carrying out taxable supplies in Luxembourg. 2) Submit Form 1 (Demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) electronically via MyGuichet to the AEDT, annexing the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société), proof of identity of the general partner (commandité) and the registered office/correspondent in Luxembourg, expected date of commencement of taxable activities, and any foreign VAT identification evidence. 3) AEDT issues a VAT identification number in the national format LU + 8 digits (TVA LU00000000), which is linked to the LBR matricule. 4) The SCSp must simultaneously obtain an EORI number (format LU + 8 digits, identical stem to the VAT number) for customs/export operations. 5) For foreign managers or non-resident general partners, a Luxembourg tax representative may be required for VAT compliance; a written power of attorney must be filed with the AEDT. 6) The entity must complete periodic VAT registrations and, where turnover thresholds are exceeded, intra-EU recapitulative statements and Intrastat declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) has no separate legal personality and is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT) and net wealth tax; the partnership's income, gains and assets are imputed to the partners pro rata under their respective tax status. Notably, the SCSp is nevertheless treated as a separate 'taxable person' for VAT purposes under the Luxembourg VAT Law, so the SCSp itself must register for VAT, issue VAT invoices and file periodic VAT returns in respect of its manufacturing and sale of surgical laparoscopy towers, notwithstanding its pass-through treatment for income tax. if the SCSp engages in commercial activity, it can be individually liable to municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal), with the tax computed at partnership level but effectively allocable among the partners; the entity may also be required to register for payroll withholding if it employs staff.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not apply a US-style 'check-the-box' regime; partnership transparency is ex lege and cannot be overridden for income tax purposes, although the foreign qualification of the SCSp as opaque can give rise to hybrid mismatch rules under EU ATAD (implemented in the Luxembourg Income Tax Law). Available elections include: (i) election to form a VAT group ('assujetti unique') under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, subject to prior AEDT approval; (ii) option to tax real estate rental under Article 44 of the VAT Law, where the SCSp owns property used in the manufacturing facility; (iii) election for joint corporate tax filing/fiscal unity under Article 164bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law — only available to fully taxable resident companies, not to an SCSp; (iv) optional VAT reverse charge for imports and certain intra-EU acquisitions under Articles 47 et seq. of the VAT Law; (v) small-enterprise franchise election under Article 57 of the VAT Law where annual turnover is below EUR 35,000, subject to the non-application of the franchise to exports and to non-resident taxable persons; (vi) hybrid mismatch transparency position statement, whereby the Luxembourg tax administration may be requested to confirm the transparent classification of the SCSp in relation to a specific foreign jurisdiction to prevent double taxation or double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the modified Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general de minimis turnover threshold for a manufacturing exporter: registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable activity. A domestic small-enterprise franchise (régime de la franchise) exempts resident established taxable persons whose annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (exclusive of VAT), but the franchise does not apply to non-resident taxable persons and does not cover export transactions where zero-rating must be claimed. The manufacturing of surgical laparoscopy towers (ISIC 3250 / HS 9018) conducted through an SCSp therefore requires immediate Luxembourg VAT registration, EORI registration, and customs presence irrespective of projected turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance (CTC), digital stamping or continuous transaction control exists in Luxembourg for B2B invoicing. Mandatory electronic obligations include: (i) B2G e-invoicing to the Luxembourg State and public sector entities via the PEPPOL network with structured formats (UBL / Factur-X) since 1 January 2021; (ii) mandatory electronic filing of periodic VAT returns, recapitulative statements (DEB), and Intrastat declarations through the e-File / MyGuichet platform; (iii) invoicing under Article 74 of the VAT Law requiring full authenticity of origin, integrity of content and legibility, with archival for 10 years; (iv) transmission of customs export declarations via the EU ECS system with MRN confirmation; (v) optional use of EDI or qualified e-signature as accepted authenticity controls; there is no additional API-based stamping requirement for the medical-device export supply chain.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero per cent VAT applies to the permanent export of goods (including Ultra-HD 4K minimally invasive rigid endoscopes and laparoscopic towers) outside the EU, pursuant to Articles 42 et seq. of the Luxembourg VAT Law, where all of the following cumulative conditions are met: (1) physical export from the EU is completed and evidenced by a valid customs export declaration (EX-A / ECS) bearing the Luxembourg EORI number; (2) the risk of loss or damage is effectively transferred to the non-EU buyer under the underlying sale contract (SWIFT LC / TT payment, Incoterms such as FOB, CIF, CIP or DAP) before the VAT liability arises; (3) the goods are transported to a third country within the administrative evidence window (Luxembourg administrative practice: normally 3 months, extendable up to 6 months in justified cases; the 180-day benchmark below constitutes the documented due-diligence standard for refund acceleration); (4) the seller's records convincingly demonstrate the actual destination and the commercial reality of the export, including transport documents issued in the name of the seller or the seller's agent; (5) for services directly related to and ancillary to the exported towers (installation supervision, commissioning, and end-user training at the non-EU hospital), zero-rating is available where the customer is a non-EU taxable person and the benefit of the services is localized outside the EU; (6) the VAT invoice must show the statutory mention 'Exonération – exportation article 42' and the AEDT may require a written confirmation of export from the buyer or its customs broker.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — EX-A / ECS computerized declaration with MRN (Movement Reference Number), Luxembourg EORI number, commodity code per the surgical-laparoscopy product classification (HS 9018 / 8528 subcomponents as applicable), declared VAT position 0.00, and actual exit office within the EU.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR — transport contract evidencing physical departure from EU territory, route, container or airwaybill reference, consignee in the non-EU country, and cross-reference to the customs MRN and commercial invoice.

Inward Remittance Certificate — documentary banking evidence of the export sales proceeds, such as SWIFT MT103 credit advice, LC settlement record, or TT wire confirmation showing receipt of the foreign currency proceeds by the SCSp's account; under Luxembourg VAT practice this is part of the commercial-diligence bundle used by AEDT on refund audits, although an EU member state may not lawfully impose a substantive 180-day repatriation condition as a validity requirement of the VAT zero-rating.

Commercial invoice and packing list — signed commercial invoice containing the export-exemption reference, full description of the Ultra-HD 4K laparoscopy towers, unit values, Incoterms, packing list, insurance certificate if any, and the buyer's purchase order.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT audit scrutiny of export zero-rating for surgical-hardware manufacturers is intensive: inspectors cross-check the ECS customs declarations, MRN status, transport manifest, insurance files, and bank statements against the SWIFT LC / TT proceeds credited to the SCSp. Where export evidence is incomplete or inconsistent, the AEDT recharacterizes the supply as taxable and reassesses VAT at 17%, applying late-payment interest (statutory rate: 0.6% per month, or the periodically published statutory interest variant) from the original return due date. Penalties escalate as follows: (i) administrative non-fraud penalties up to EUR 10,000 under the general tax law; (ii) fraud penalties of up to the amount of tax evaded, with exclusion of refund claims; (iii) criminal sanctions for deliberate VAT fraud pursuant to Articles 127–128 of the VAT Law, carrying imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 25,000 per invoice batch; (iv) retrospective clawback of refunded VAT, compounded by the 17% re-assessed VAT, interest, and penalties, and sustained by joint and several liability of the general partner (commandité) and any tax representative of the SCSp; (v) the taxpayer must retain all export documentation for 10 years, as the absence of records creates a rebuttable presumption against zero-rating. Luxembourg applies the 180-day repatriation benchmark as an administrative due-diligence and refund-acceleration cut-off, although it is not a formal statutory validity condition of the exemption under EU law; non-repatriation within 180 days without commercial justification will materially heighten audit scrutiny and the risk of ECS-exit refusal or reverse-charge reassessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); supranational monetary authority is the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential banking supervision by Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible; Luxembourg applies unrestricted capital and current account movements under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC. No prior authorisation, surrender requirement, or FX licensing applies to profit remittance, capital repatriation, trade settlement, or loan servicing. Payments are limited only by EU/UN sanctions screening, CSSF financial-sanctions guidance, and AML/CFT obligations under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 as amended; corporate outflows are governed by corporate-law distribution tests (Luxembourg law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended) and tax substance, not FX control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export-proceeds surrender rule or mandatory conversion ratio exists in Luxembourg; exporters may retain export proceeds in EUR or any foreign currency in BCL-supervised bank accounts without restriction. Cross-border movements must be recorded by the reporting bank under ECB Balance of Payments / BCL VAD statistical reporting and under Regulation (EU) 2015/847, including originator and beneficiary data for every wire transfer; cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more require a customs declaration under Regulation (EU) 2018/1672.

Operational EUR/USD Settlement and LC Trade Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE/Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Trade Account with e-Banking, FX & LC Lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: MEDIUM-HIGH for EU-authorised/PSD2-passported Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) operating in Luxembourg (e.g., CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported payment/electronic-money institutions). EMIs are viable as supplementary multi-currency settlement wallets for trade receivables and vendor disbursements, but are legally incapable of holding deposits, issuing commercial letters of credit, or providing credit lines under the Luxembourg Law of 10 November 2009 on payment services and the EU PSD2 framework. Capital escrow and LC-backed trade flows must therefore remain with a Tier-1 Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg AML law and CSSF Regulation 12-02 do not mandate physical director attendance; remote onboarding is permissible through eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures, CSSF-accepted video KYC identity verification, and certified document transmission. In practice, Tier-1 banks routinely require either an in-person kick-off meeting in Luxembourg for the general partner (SCSp requires representation by a Luxembourg-resident/general partner) or a notarised/apostilled power of attorney, UBO certification, and board resolution; full remote opening is feasible where the general partner is a Luxembourg professional (e.g., a corporate services provider) and all UBOs pass enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp transparency and UBO validation (partnership treated as transparent; beneficial ownership of all limited partners above the 25% threshold must be evidenced).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) UBO declaration per Law of 13 January 2019, certified partnership agreement and RCS extract, organisational chart and tax residence of each UBO, passport copies, and sworn source-of-funds statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident offshore limited partners or complex multi-layer holding chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank reference letters, audited financial statements of upstream entities, commercial rationale presentation, substance file including administration place, office lease, and Luxembourg-resident general partner mandate, plus tax-residency certificates from all partner jurisdictions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade flows and intra-group technical/royalty transfers (medical equipment supply chain with high invoice values).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase orders, customs declarations, bills of lading, transport insurance certificates, CE/MDR 2017/745 conformity documentation, lender/buyer verification, and transfer-pricing documentation supporting the invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions/PEP exposure in sales counterparties or receiving banks (emerging-market distributors of surgical laparoscopy towers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List screening results, PEP declarations, KYC counterparty packs, UN/EU jurisdiction clearance, end-user attestation, and export licence confirmation required under EU Dual-Use Regulation (EU) 2021/821 if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity/loan capital to the SCSp is routed by SWIFT MT103 (USD) or SEPA Credit Transfer / Target2 (EUR) to the escrow account. Wire instructions must state the entity's BCL VAD/ECB statistical purpose code for direct investment (subscription to partnership capital), the SCSp's trade registry reference, and the CSSF-standard AML reference; the remitting bank must be a non-sanctioned bank with an identifiable correspondent under SWIFT gpi rules. Same-day availability requires pre-validation of the source-of-funds dossier and compatibility with the account's standing debit limits.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements execute via SWIFT MT103/MT202 for telegraphic transfers; supplier payments for surgical laparoscopy tower components use SEPA/SEPA Instant for EUR and MT103 for USD. Large-value export transactions with hospitals/distributors are cleared through Commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP600: MT700 issuance, MT710/720 confirmation, and MT754 advice with presentation of invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, bill of lading, insurance certificate, and health-technology conformity dossier; proceeds are settled to the operational account, with surplus FX converted by the corporate FX line rather than costly cash conversion.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/USD outright forward contracts (plain vanilla).
EUR/USD FX swaps and reciprocal basis swaps for rollover risk management.
EUR/USD cross-currency interest-rate swaps for matching medium-term equipment-finance liabilities.
Offshore CNY/CNH deliverable forwards and EUR/CNH options for China-origin component payments (no RMB NDF required because CNH forwards are deliverable).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in restricted, non-convertible emerging-market currencies strictly to hedge underlying commercial/trade receivables or payables, supported by treasury policy and trade documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts deposition (dépôt des comptes annuels) of the SCSp with the Luxembourg trade and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) under the Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following year; the exemption under Article 9 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 applies only if all partners are natural persons and the SCSp does not elect legal personality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: LBR reminder and formal notice; referral to the Public Prosecutor; court-imposed fine and judicial strike-off (radiation) of the SCSp on persistent default; the general partner (associé gérant) is exposed to personal liability and disqualification proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (confirmation annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs) of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs — RBE), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year; confirmation due within 30 days after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; any change in ultimate beneficial ownership, including partnership interest transfers, must be declared within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties for the general partner and managers, including fines and imprisonment for wilful omission or false declarations; administrative blocking of distributions and adverse AML/KYC consequences for the entity's banking relationships

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg income tax return of the SCSp (déclaration fiscale annuelle) and net-wealth-tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration), local tax office (bureau d'imposition) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, the return is due no later than 31 December of the following tax year when filed with an approved tax adviser; accelerated paper deadlines apply; the tax-transparent SCSp files to record the allocation of taxable income to its partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of up to 10% of taxes due plus default interest; ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office) by the ACD; the general partner may be jointly liable for filing defaults

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit by a Luxembourg-approved auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) is compulsory for an SCSp which exceeds two of the three criteria: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, or an average of 50 employees; audit is also mandatory if required by the partnership agreement, by a regulated fund regime (e.g., SIF/RAIF), or by the LBR authorities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for individual annual accounts and mandatory for any consolidated accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner (associé gérant) must review the RBE file at least annually and confirm its accuracy; a transfer of partnership interests or admission of a new limited partner (commanditaire) does not automatically update the RBE — a fresh declaration must be filed within 15 days so that the register discloses the ultimate beneficial owner of the transferred interest
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,100 – 2,700 per annum for a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent and corporate secretarial provider (EUR 1,000 – 2,500)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,500 – 16,500 per annum for a certified Luxembourg audit (EUR 4,000 – 15,000) of a small to mid-size SCSp

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
